citation: Glessner House Museum, 'The Glessners and their servants', The Story of a House (blog), 15 October 2012.
author: Glessner House Museum
locator: The whole post: the live-in staff of eight the house was planned for; the live-in women (cook, waitress, parlor maid, ladies' maid) and the daily laundress and seamstress; the men's rooms over the coach house and the women's over the kitchen wing, each with its own Eighteenth Street entrance; the staff dinner about 3 p.m.; the kitchen annunciator; the iceman's half-door; the dovecotes; six stalls and as many carriages; the change to automobiles in 1906.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-08 (T-3525) through a fetch that returned a summary of the post's text with short quoted segments. No archived snapshot verified.
note: The house museum's account of how the staff lived and worked in the house, written from the building and Frances Glessner's servants' journal. Later scholarship by the institution that holds the papers. It names no servant.
